text:
Martin (support): quick heads-up — AcmeApps reporting failures from our embeddings endpoint after the model catalog update this AM. They get a 400 with body `{'error':'vector_length_mismatch','expected':1536,'received':1024}` when calling the model name they had pinned.

Joan (csm): AcmeApps-prod is blocked (traffic ~27k calls/day). They can reproduce in staging by calling the same `model` value. Customer says they explicitly pinned `rwd-embed-large` (no version suffix).

Alice Wang (eng-ml): can you paste the raw request/response (headers + body) and whether they were using batching? also which SDK version?

Martin (support): pasted curl from customer: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-large","input":"the quick brown fox"}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request`
```
{"error":"vector_length_mismatch","expected":1536,"received":1024}
```
No batching on that call; they tried a small batch later and saw identical error. Using our js-sdk 2.4.1.

Samir Patel (infra): quick diagnosis: during the last rollout we introduced a new embed variant (v2) optimized for latency with a 1024-dim output. We updated the alias `rwd-embed-large` to point at the new variant as part of the rollout. Pinning to the alias (just the model name) does NOT pin you to a rev — aliases can be remapped. Looks like Acme pinned the alias, and when the alias flipped they started receiving 1024-dim vectors which broke their consumer expecting 1536.

Alice Wang (eng-ml): ack. so root cause = alias remap + customer assumption that alias is stable. We should: (1) offer immediate rollback for affected customers, (2) add a server-side error that explains "model revision mismatch" more clearly, (3) update support KB to recommend pinning to exact revision (e.g., `rwd-embed-large@20260112`).

Samir Patel (infra): I'm creating INC-2026-45 to track. For immediate mitigation I can revert the alias mapping for Acme's tenant and re-route them to the old revision. Planning to do this now in the config plane; it should be instant.

InfraBot: INC-2026-45 created and assigned to Samir Patel. Pinged oncall. :eyes:

Martin (support): Can you also confirm whether any cache/batching layer could have mixed dimensions (i.e., older kv cache stuck to new model)? Acme's stack uses our prefix caching.

Samir Patel (infra): caching wouldn't change vector length — the runtime returns whatever the model emits. However, if they cached vectors in their app under an assumption of 1536 dims, they would fail when reading a 1024-dim vector back into that code. We verified our KV cache logic still keys on model_revision + input hash, so it shouldn't cross-wire revisions. The underlying mistake is the alias remap.

Alice Wang (eng-ml): to help customers detect this proactively, here's a tiny check they can run after creating an embedding: 
```
# python example
resp = client.embeddings.create(model='rwd-embed-large', input='foo')
vec = resp.data[0].embedding
if len(vec) != EXPECTED_DIMS:
    raise RuntimeError(f"embedding length {len(vec)} != expected {EXPECTED_DIMS}")
```
Share this snippet in KB. Also adding a short curl-based smoke test that asserts `len(embedding)` before consuming.

Samir Patel (infra): Revert done for Acme alias mapping. I've also gated the alias updates behind a canary that excludes customers with explicit alias pins for the next 48h. Will run a small audit to list other tenants pinned to aliases.

Joan (csm): Acme confirmed in staging and then prod — their ingest pipeline is green. They said revert fixed the issue. :white_check_mark: They want a note about how to pin to an immutable revision.

Martin (support): Customer verified successful calls: `HTTP/1.1 200` + embedding of length 1536. Closing the immediate support ticket.

Alice Wang (eng-ml): follow-ups: (a) docs/KB update showing alias vs revision and examples for pinning, (b) change error payload to include both `expected_dim` and `received_dim` with clearer message, (c) internal runbook for model alias rollbacks. I'll own the error payload change.

Samir Patel (infra): noted. I'll produce the list of tenants that have alias-only pins and propose a migration path (script to recommend `model@rev`). Also adding a telemetry alert for sudden spikes in `vector_length_mismatch` errors.

Martin (support): logging action items in the support ticket and will send the KB snippets to Acme. Thanks team.

InfraBot: Incident INC-2026-45 status=resolved, note="alias revert for tenant acme-apps applied"

Joan (csm): recording postmortem notes in the customer record and scheduling a 1:1 to explain pinning best practices.

Alice Wang (eng-ml): lesson learned: treat alias remaps as a breaking change for customers who pin the alias. We'll update rollout playbook. :memo:
